sentences.text: Sinornithosaurus is a genus of feathered dromaeosaurid dinosaur, a name that translates to 'Chinese bird-lizard'.
This animal belonged to the family Dromaeosauridae, a group of agile predators known for possessing a distinctive sickle-shaped claw on their toes.
It was among the smallest members of its family, reaching a length of about 90 centimeters, and featured proportionally very long arms and hands.
The holotype, which is the specimen the species is based on, measured 1.2 meters long and weighed between 3 and 5 kilograms.
Sinornithosaurus holds the distinction of being the first dromaeosaurid dinosaur discovered with feathers.
Its discovery in 1999 caused a sensation because it was the fifth non-avian dinosaur with feathers to be identified by that date.
Analysis of microscopic cell structures suggests the animal had black and rufous feathers, while later studies indicated colors like yellow, gray, and black scattered across its body.

The genus Sinornithosaurus and the type species Sinornithosaurus millenii were described by Xu Xing, Wang Xiaolin, and Wu Xiaochun of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing in 1999.
A second species, S. haoiana, meaning 'Chinese Hao bird-lizard', was described by Liu et al. in 2004 based on a specimen differing from S. millenii in head and hip characters.
The presence of feathers in this animal suggests that other running dromaeosaurids, such as Velociraptor, may also have possessed feathers.
Some scientists suggest Sinornithosaurus could have glided for short distances after leaping from trees.
Turner, Makovicky, and Norell concluded that specimen NGMC 91 was a subadult individual of Sinornithosaurus millenii.
Phylogenetic analysis by Xu Xing demonstrated that Sinornithosaurus is basal or primitive among dromaeosaurs.
The parent group of Sinornithosaurus is Microraptorinae.
Sinornithosaurus millenii lived approximately 125 million years ago during the Barremian age of the Early Cretaceous, making it one of the earliest known dromaeosaurids.
Fossils of Sinornithosaurus haoiana and the specimen NGMC 91 date to approximately 122 million years ago.
Sinornithosaurus lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
Turner, Makovicky, and Norell in 2012 argued that the supposed distinctive features of S. haoiana are present in S. millenii or vary among Sinornithosaurus specimens.
In 2009, a team led by Empu Gong suggested Sinornithosaurus was the first identified venomous dinosaur based on grooved teeth and a possible venom gland cavity.
Longrich and Currie (2009) expressed the opinion that Sinornithosaurus was probably too heavy to fly.
